questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was interested in going to a country that spoke Italian. I wanted to try and live within the italian culture for a semester and learn as much Italian as possible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I remember it as being allright.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not that much, there was a zoom meeting with some information, but other than that you had to seek the information much yourself, but they answer quite quickly on the mails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I had a very easy time finding housing as I found it through some familiar contacts, but it was quite expensive though as I lived alone in an apartment, which is very rare. Everyone I met lived with other people, even some were two in one room. 

You should start as soon as possible starting to find housing, as it is a crazy market in Bologna. Everyone found housing, but was through different portals, some AirBnb, some private, some Facebook, therefore different prices and locations aswell.

If you are very early I've also heard about the student hotels, which were recommended by some.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is not much as "off" or "on" campus in Bologna, the campus is placed different places throughout the city. But I lived 1.5 km outside the city walls to the east. The city walls are the ring road that go around the center of Bologna, and often you talk about center as being within those. You will be there the most of your time, but there are some nice places outside of it aswell. I did not mind living outside the center. Everyone bikes around in Bologna, as it is really flat, so if you live a km or two outside the center, you will be fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it as being fairly easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I dont remember.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: This is the thing particular about Bologna. I was succesful in registering classes, you complete your study plan on their student portal "studenti online" and then you take the courses. You don't have to register classes before they start, you can just join multiple classes and then see how it is. I completed my study plan after starting the classes and then you register for the classes completely when you are going to exam.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When looking at your courses you will probably have classes that overlap, it is very difficult to figure out a schedule where they don't overlap. I had some overlaps, but ended up being fine, then I just went to a class one week and the other the other week.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had mostly master classes, and the level was not that high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In my experience the teachers were sitting at their desk throughout the lecture talking throughout the whole lecture. I was not that fond of the teaching style.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: History of Mass Communication, Viticulture, Urban Agriculture, Introduction to Italian Culture & Non-Western Multilingual Comparative Research.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend Urban Agriculture, it is quite interesting topics, and I am not sure if they will do it again, but we wen't visiting interesting projects in Bologna and had a five day field trip to Venice paid by the school. So if that is part of it again I recommend it very much!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I bought a bike for 80 euro. When I changed from shopping in COOP to Lidl I saved so much money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
As an Erasmus student you can get a TPER card which gives access to the bus in Bologna and costs 10 euro for your whole erasmus semester, very cheap! 
I bought a bike for 70 euro, watch out you don't buy a stolen one. 
I bought a sim-card at Iliad for 10 euro as well with 150 gb a month, as i didn't have wifi in my house.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As a part of ESN there was volleyball and basketball every saturday. I heard it was fun. Other than that a football tournament during the semester. But in the ESN whatsapp groups it was easy organizing some activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a lot going on in Bologna. It is a student city and a lot of events are happening all the time. I was at a wine festival in Bologna, and there are music and concerts going on as well. Follow bologna_parvenza on instagram, they put up a "what is going on in Bologna" every weekend and sometimes in the weekdays.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Bologna is quite central and from Bologna you can visit some parts of Italy. I had some friends who had cars here and I enjoyed very much to go on few trips around Bologna. I highly recommend to go hiking Via degli Dei, which is a hiking route from Bologna to Firenze of 130 km. You can do it by tent with some other people.
Parco di villa Ghigi is a really nice spot up in the hills above Bologna, takes one hour to walk there. Not many people go there, but you have an amazing overview over the city and a quiet park. I loved going there on weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy I think. I loved going for a cappucino and a cornetto in the mornings at a "bar" for 2.5 euro and to just eat pasta daily.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In the beginning I just wrote a Facebook post in one of the Erasmus groups if anyone wanted to go for a coffee or a beer, and a lot of people answered and we went for a coffee. Other than that in the ESN groups to begin with a lot of people are writing if anyone wants to go for something, and then you can just join. Everyone is on the same level to begin with so people are very keen to go meet people, and then groups slowly formed.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it difficult to be able to speak italian as I mostly just met other Erasmus students which I regret a bit, I would have wanted to live with some italians if I had to do it again.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The italian people in Bologna are very friendly, and aperitivo is cool.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open towards other people, try to figure out what is going on in the city, as there are so many things happening all the time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I've covered it pretty well above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: 1 euro espressos and being able to live in the Italian culture for a semester.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think most people would answer here; finding housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
